title: inGRASS: Incremental Graph Spectral Sparsification via Low-Resistance-Diameter Decomposition
problem: Incremental spectral sparsification of large undirected graphs requires scalable algorithms that can efficiently update sparse graph representations as new edges are added to dynamic graphs. Current methods lack the ability to handle rapid incremental updates with both high speed and solution quality.
motivation: Efficient graph sparsification accelerates computation across diverse applications including circuit simulation, finite element analysis, and social network processing by reducing graph size while preserving spectral properties.
method: inGRASS employs a multilevel resistance embedding framework that decomposes the initial sparsifier into node clusters with bounded effective-resistance diameters using a low-resistance-diameter (LRD) decomposition scheme. The setup phase operates in nearly-linear time to identify spectrally-critical edges and eliminate redundant ones. The update phase leverages low-dimensional node embeddings to efficiently assess edge importance and enable O(log N) time incremental updates for each new edge.
key_novelty: Low-resistance-diameter decomposition scheme that enables scalable parallel sparsification with incremental O(log N) per-edge updates through resistance-based clustering.
contributions: Novel inGRASS algorithm combining multilevel resistance embedding with efficient incremental updates
Low-resistance-diameter decomposition framework for identifying spectrally-critical edges
Near-linear time setup phase with O(log N) incremental update complexity
Demonstrated 200× speedups on circuit, finite element, and social network graphs
